title: Youth Slang, Street Register, and Subcultural Jargon: bevállal, kiakad, rákattan

sections.title: Metaphorical Extension in Slang Verbs
sections.content: Hungarian youth slang generates new expressive vocabulary largely through preverbal metaphor. Standard spatial verbs take on psychological and social connotations: 'bevállal' (to take on a challenge, dare to commit to something risky), 'kiakad' (literally 'to unhook/jam', colloquially to freak out, lose one's temper, or be appalled), and 'rákattan' (literally 'to click onto', colloquially to become hooked or obsessed with something).

sections.title: Sociolinguistic Boundaries and Communicative Competence
sections.content: Nouns like 'duma' (smooth talk, chatter, banter, or empty rhetoric) and verbs like 'átlát' (to see through someone's pretenses or fathom a complex system) bridge colloquial street talk and informal peer interactions. Achieving B2 competence means understanding these vivid figures of speech when native speakers use them in casual settings, while recognizing where their usage would be inappropriate (such as academic essays or formal administration).

sections.title: Popular Contemporary Colloquial and Slang Terms
rows: Ki merné bevállalni az előadást a beteg kolléga helyett? (Who would dare take on the presentation?)
Teljesen kiakadt, amikor meglátta a horribilis számlát. (He totally freaked out when he saw the bill.)
A fiatalok azonnal rákattantak az új videójátékra. (The young people instantly got hooked on the new game.)
Gyorsan átlátja a legbonyolultabb helyzeteket is. (He sees through even the most complex situations quickly.)
Hagyd a felesleges dumát, térjünk a lényegre! (Cut the idle chatter, let's get down to business!)

items.spanish: Nem mindenki meri bevállalni azt a kockázatot, amivel egy induló startup vezetése jár.
items.english: Not everyone dares take on the risk involved in running an early-stage startup.

items.spanish: A professzor teljesen kiakadt, amikor a diákok puskázni próbáltak a vizsgán.
items.english: The professor completely freaked out when the students tried to cheat on the exam.

items.spanish: A lány annyira rákattant a magyar irodalomra, hogy naponta kiolvas egy könyvet.
items.english: The girl got so hooked on Hungarian literature that she finishes a book every day.

items.spanish: A tapasztalt nyomozó azonnal átlátta a gyanúsított ravasz trükkjeit.
items.english: The experienced investigator immediately saw through the suspect's cunning tricks.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: While 'bevállal' is widely used even in contemporary media interviews, avoid using 'duma' or 'kiakad' in formal correspondence. Replace 'bevállal' with 'elvállal' or 'felvállal', 'kiakad' with 'megdöbben' or 'felháborodik', and 'duma' with 'érvelés' or 'beszéd'.
